answer.rationale: p99 latency is elevated on the write path during settlement peak. Rollback is blocked by compliance requirement on security patch. Regional failover risks context loss during peak writes. Adding capacity is slower and requires coordination. Routing read-heavy operations (particularly dashboard/reporting queries per memory_b5) to read replicas can immediately reduce primary load without touching the release. This preserves the mandatory security patch, protects write availability during settlement peak, and is reversible. memory_b5 demonstrates this exact pattern worked to recover transactional latency same-day. A standard experiment scope isolates impact while we monitor whether read replica routing alone suffices, or if subsequent capacity/failover becomes necessary in the next window.
